reading_rules.text: Stage 4 starts from the observations, not the verses (researcher, #2526 Q7, 2026-11-21): the subgroups and the stage 3 observations on them are the input, the behaviours are discovered from analysing them, and the base data is read back into only occasionally. Every finding of step 3.1 or 3.2 rests on named observations (a traced node on each, with an occurrence node as well) and its occurrence nodes lie within the occurrences those observations cover; an occurrence outside them is allowed only where the finding records a read-back (the verse and why). Each node has a role from reading.node_roles other than lexical, chosen by the reading. A 3.3 finding carries nodes on the occurrences of both sides in the shared verses.

A finding of a stage 4 row is checked by the rules of observationrecord.check and check_item_parts (kind, text, basis, route, parts.item and what the item needs, node roles, collection of each node) and by RG, RW and RS, which are not restated here: one observation for each finding, never a duplicate, with a node on each word it applies to (RO11, RW-03); founded in the observations and never a restatement of the verse (B:131); parts.item is one of the items the row's item uses (cfg_setting layer.reading). An observation whose nodes all bear on an act is refused: those words are nodes of the observation of the act. A finding is a building block of a behaviour and never a claim (stage 5).

Nothing the step reads is lost on the way to stage 5. Step 3.1: every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared in not_used with its reason in words. Step 3.2: every 3.1 observation of the collection is gathered into a behaviour (a traced node on it from a flag finding of type discovery) or declared in not_gathered with its reason, and the row has at least one behaviour unless it is recorded as none with its reason. A behaviour names and gathers; it makes no claim about what the behaviour is.

An earlier inner-being observation with a node on the occurrences of a 3.1 row (any stage but lexical, layer-1, layer-2 and layer-3) is shown in the pull for information and may be actioned in `existing`: accepted, modified, deleted, merged or left, each with its reason, through observationrecord (RW-01, RW-09); nothing is demanded of it, and it counts for nothing in the check. A row answered again withdraws its earlier observations with the reason.
One observation per finding, never a duplicate description; a finding applying to several verses or words carries several nodes, each with the word's role in it.

Read outward from the verse, not inward from the scope's question. First record everything the verse carries, each with where it bears (chapter, thread, signpost); answer the scope's question last. A verse often has two or three significances, and none is dropped.
Read the verse in its passage and genre; name the speaker; explore figures for what they say about the inner being; take paired and opposite acts together. Restating a verse is not reading it.

Find the main inner-being operation, and give every word that bears on it its role in this finding (cfg_setting reading.node_roles): characteristic, qualifier and what it gives the characteristic, object or content, relational target, or enactment. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being is standalone. The role comes from this verse, never from the cluster tag. Where a standalone word proves to qualify a characteristic, it is a qualifier of it.

A qualifier gets no separate account of itself, but what it gives the characteristic it binds to is evaluated for its value and recorded as a qualification finding, applied by its nodes to the qualifier (role qualifier) and the characteristic (role characteristic). What it gives can vary widely: grade, nature, impact, size, relation, a measure, strengthening, ground, cause, object, setting or bait are examples, not a list (#2273 D9). A qualifier whose usage varies across contexts may earn its own reading later.
Record how the M-code words work together (a relational observation). Record any pointer outside the verse separately, without resolving it inline.

Record the parties: who bears the act, who causes it, who is acted on (source, target, impact, purpose), and the route (cfg_enum observation_route). A non-human being is never itself a HIB; a collective stays one HIB; an implied party is named as referential, never asserted.
Read the T3 operations, movement and force, negators (a refusal is an act), connectives, body parts, places, objects and nature for what they carry here; read every row, untagged ones too.

For every word that names an inner or bodily act, look at the original: the root's range in all three meaning sources read together, never one picked and the others dropped; the ESV renderings across its verses; whether the English adds or hides; the literal sense beside the rendering. Where more than one reading is open, record each, and mark the choice 'I read'.

Record each relevant word's face as it appears HERE: the circumstance in this verse and where the sense departs from the general gloss. Identifying and clarifying the face is lexical work; what the faces do for the inner being, and a double meaning in different scenarios, are layer 2 of the collection reading (layer-aspects-are-ledgered-and-never-left-open).
Never close a verse or item on 'not X'. A role label is never a verdict; the close records what the verse is. Silence about the inner being is a finding, recorded as data with its reason.
A phenomenon hidden behind a stated or refrained act may be named, with the verb, clause or stated silence that grounds it, and whether it is stated or read.
A literary or structural pattern is not an inner-being observation: log it as an open question instead. A human/divine comparison is recorded only where the text's own wording anchors it.
Keep the source of an interior state apart from the source of an enablement to act.
Morph is read, not carried: where occurrences of a word show different stems or voices, record whether the subject does, undergoes or causes the act.
A difference, or a specific inference, is its own observation, never folded into another.

A word that is only a homonym or a name, with no meaningful context, is recorded as such (tag no-human-context) and left. Data errors found while reading are flagged (tag data-error), not fixed in the reading.
The question catalogue's questions are prompts for the areas to explore. A question that does not apply is not answered, and no answer is manufactured beyond what the verse shows.
Faculty (heart, soul, spirit, mind) is reflected on at the end, over the scope, not per word.
Before reading the whole scope, read a few verses and have them checked.
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.

A reading records findings of eight kinds (cfg_setting reading.observation_parts; the kind is the tag): face, qualification, party, statement, link, use, term, silence. A finding holds its text, meaning, implication, basis, its structured parts (ib_observation.parts: item, and mode, polarity, flag_type or grounds where its item needs them; reading.observation_items) and, on a party or link finding, its route; its nodes hold the verse, the word, the occurrence, the collection and its subgroup, the word's role in the finding and the reading that applied it. The silence kind is not used by Analysis_phase_1: a surface with no inner-being role is not recorded.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
An observation about a word can be answered only by consulting this occurrence's verse, span and morph.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.

A flag raised in reading (needs adjacent context, a pointer) states its reason and what the follow-up must establish, and is carried to an open item, not resolved inline. Can't-resolve is recorded, never guessed (tag could-not-resolve).
Where the evidence points to more than one reading, each is its own observation with its own evidence.
A re-read includes the observations already recorded for the verse, so the reading sees prior findings and builds on them.
Where a verse ends up for a finding is recorded on the node (ib_node.disposition, cfg_enum observation_disposition: told, claim, held, data, context, withdrawn), with its reason or carrier.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

After recording, every observation is read back against the verse for sense. An uncertain one is recorded as uncertain (tag could-not-resolve, or basis read: 'I read'), never asserted. A rule found to be systematically wrong is raised as a config change with the learning, never worked round in the reading.

A word is read per its lettered Strong's code (its grain), never the bare lemma (B:113). The occurrences of a word with several senses are related per grain and never aggregated across grains: related verses are same-grain occurrences.

Content words carry the inner-being impact and are read even when no cluster tags them. Function words (particles, prepositions, conjunctions, suffixes, pronouns) get no observation of their own, except negators and connectives, which are read for what they do (RG-07). A T2 word never stands alone: it is read as the qualifier of what it binds to.

The words in cfg_setting reading.non_characteristic_strongs are never a verse's characteristic: superscription metadata and named external adversaries. They are read as standalone or as qualifiers. The list is per word, not per cluster, because a cluster can hold both kinds.

A tagged word that works adverbially in an occurrence (a noun with a preposition qualifying the predicate, as 'in the counsel of the wicked') is a qualifier there, not the verse's characteristic. The role is per occurrence: the same word may be the characteristic elsewhere.
In a simile, the predicates of the vehicle (the tree that yields, does not wither) are read for what they say of the one compared (the tenor), not as the vehicle's own acts.

An existing observation counts for a surface when its node names that occurrence (verse_lexical_id), or, with none, when the node's verse, Strong and surface match one occurrence only. A node that names a verse and no surface, or matches more than one occurrence, is set aside: it does not count for any surface.

When a verse is worked, every existing observation and node on it, of any stage, is checked against the verse by its wording. The stage is not an indication of the nature of an observation and is never used to filter. Each observation is accepted, modified (changed in place; the old value, the new value and the reason are kept in ib_observation_change), soft deleted (the `deleted` column, with the reason), merged (a duplicate description, into the observation that is kept) or, when its wording shows it is not verse understanding, left exactly as it is with the reason. The check's fixes are part of it and need no separate approval. Nothing is physically deleted.

A surface with no inner-being role in a verse has no observation of its own. A word read in the verse that holds nothing for the inner being has the role standalone, which is a role and not an absence; where it could be a qualifier it is read as the qualifier of the characteristic it serves.

The observations of a verse state what the verse shows, and Record enforces it from cfg_setting reading.observation_rules and reading.observation_items: an observation of a relevant surface carries parts.item (one of the nine items), is written as one of the kinds that item allows, on a basis the item allows (a read observation names its grounds), and carries what its item needs (polarity, mode, flag type; a party carries its route). The words that bear on an act are nodes of the observation of the act, never an observation of their own (bears_on_only_refused). Every surface with the role characteristic has each applicable item observed or stated absent with the reason; the verse always has an operation observation. A verse whose observations do not comply is not recorded (#2329).

For every surface with the role characteristic, the nine items of spec 4.2 (reading.observation_items) are each explored, and each applicable item is its own observation (parts.item), written once and applied to every characteristic it is true of by its nodes; a qualifier or shared observation carries nodes on every characteristic it covers. An item the verse does not show gets no observation and is stated absent on the surface (items_absent) with the reason; the meaning item is never absent. The operation item carries a mode (done, foreseen, commanded, negated, reported) and an action description of who or what does what, read from before and after as the verse itself states them (passage-level before and after are the claims process's); the verse always has an operation observation. A read observation (basis read) names its grounds in the words of the verse (parts.grounds). No observation restates the verse text (no run of more than reading.observation_items max_verse_words_copied words). The same text for all items is not an exploration of them. Which word is the characteristic is the verse's decision, never the cluster's (RG-03). The nuance pointers (reading.nuance_pointers) say where each nuance is recorded (#2329).

rows.group: what the mind holds or produces: a thought, view or device
rows.asks: What do the stage 3 observations of this subgroup (its definition, its Strong's enrichment, its pairings, qualifiers, entities, direction, relations and double meanings, with the stage 1 senses) show of the elements of a behaviour of the inner being: what is done and its mode, whether a refusal or a pursuit, what it is directed at, the outward act, the other party with the route, the circumstance, the chain of operations, and the dimensions of the working (what a qualifier or a variation of the word gives it, from the lexical variation the stage 3 observations record)? Each finding is one observation that rests on named observations (a traced node on each) and carries nodes on the occurrences those observations cover, with the role each has; an occurrence outside them is allowed only with a read-back (the verse and why). Every stage 3 observation of the subgroup is rested on by a finding or declared not used, with the reason. A finding is a building block and never a claim about the behaviour as a whole (stage 5).

interventions: Work from the observations: the stage 3 observations of the subgroup are the input, and the verses are base data read back only where an observation does not settle the point; a read-back is recorded (the verse and why).
Read the lexical variation (the different Strong's codes of a surface, the forms of a word, the double meanings) as the dimensions of how the working happens, not as a difference to be smoothed away.
A behaviour is discovered from the elements, not assumed from the subgroup: a subgroup may form one behaviour, part of one, join others, or form none.

Record building blocks only. A statement of what a behaviour is, is a claim and belongs to stage 5; stage 5 receives the observations and not the subgroups, so everything it will need from them is recorded here.
Check the original where an observation depends on the word's range (RG-08); do not force a meaning and never close on 'not X' (RG-10).

A word whose role is not its collection's is reclassified by the collection change procedure and the step reopens (B:129, B:134); a discovery outside the observations is recorded as a flag finding of type discovery and is not resolved inline (RW-07).

Words of life stand with the group in Dan 2:30 (living, 9 before), Dan 5:10 (live, 3 before) and Heb 4:12 (living, 19 before). The distances, and the phrases (the living, live forever, the word is living), show no grammatical tie to the member.

may_rest_on_besides.text: In Pro 18:11 the rich man's wealth is called his strong city, a high wall in his imagination: the wall is in what he pictures to himself, not in fact, so maskit ('imagination, figure') names what a man holds in his own mind about his security.

In Job 32:6, 32:10 and 32:17 Elihu speaks of declaring his deah ('knowledge, opinion'): in 32:6 he was timid to declare it to the aged, in 32:10 and 32:17 he asks to be heard and will answer with his share; the word is a view he holds and means to set out in speech, not a fact he reports.

In Psa 139:23 the psalmist asks God to search him, to know his heart and to try him and know his thoughts: sarappim ('disquieting thoughts') are what stirs within him, set parallel to the heart, and he asks that God himself test and know it.

In Rom 2:15 the plural noun 'reasonings, thoughts' is the subject of the accusing or excusing that stands beside the conscience; the lexicon lists 'a thought, cogitation' for this verse, and the verse makes the thoughts the voices that judge the person.

In Act 17:29 the noun 'thought, design' in the genitive qualifies the image made by art: it is the thinking that devises it; the lexicon lists 'the result of thought, invention, device' for this verse, and the verse sets human devising against the divine being.

In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the verb 'to look at' is negated and its object is the persons: the sense is 'to look to, have regard for' what a person appears to be, which the lexicon lists for Mt 22:16 and which the ESV renders as caring about opinion; the verse adds 'not swayed by appearances'.
In Pro 18:2 the noun 'heart' is what the fool takes pleasure in laying bare: the ESV renders it his opinion, which is the inner view disclosed; the word is the heart as the holder of what he thinks.

In Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 the plural noun 'reasonings' is the first item in lists of what comes out of the heart, before the sins named after it; the sense is the reasonings that issue from the heart as a source.

In Luk 2:35, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8 and 1Cor 3:20 the plural noun 'reasonings' is what is known or revealed to another: Jesus perceives and knows what they reason, what lies in many hearts is revealed, and the Lord knows the reasonings of the wise and finds them futile; the sense is the inner line of thought, open to the one who knows it.
In Jam 2:4 the plural noun 'reasonings' is in the genitive of quality, 'judges of evil reasonings': it is the thinking by which the readers make distinctions among themselves.
In Luk 11:17 the noun 'thought' is what Jesus knows before he answers; the lexicon lists the word for this verse alone, and the sense is an inward thought known to him.

In Luk 1:51 the noun 'mind, thinking' is in the dative with the hearts: the proud are scattered in the thinking of their hearts; the lexicon gives the part of the inner person that thinks, whose seat is the heart.

In Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25 and Heb 4:12 the plural noun 'thought' is the inner content of persons that another sees: Jesus knows their thoughts, and the word of God discerns the thoughts and intentions of the heart; the sense is 'thought', set with the heart as the place.

In 2Cor 11:3 the plural noun 'minds, thoughts' is the subject of being led astray from devotion to Christ; the lexicon lists 'the heart, soul, disposition' and 'a conception of the mind' for this code, and here it is the readers' thinking.

In 1Cor 2:11 the stored word is the article ahead of the genitive 'of the man', which the ESV renders as 'thoughts'; it stands for 'the things of' the person and is not a word of thought by itself, and its morph is empty in the stored data, which is flagged as a data error (RG-16), not corrected in the reading.

In Eze 38:10 the plural noun 'words, matters' is what comes up on the heart of Gog in the verse: matters arising in his mind, which lead to the evil scheme; it is the noun for things, used here for what arises in the mind.

In Lam 3:62 the noun 'meditation, musing' (construct) stands beside the lips of the assailants and is against the speaker all day; the lexicon lists 'plotting' for the word, so it is the muttered musing of hostile people.

In Ecc 10:20 the noun 'knowledge, mind' with the preposition marks the place of the thought: even in the mind, the king is not to be cursed, set beside the bedroom; the sense is 'mind, the place of thinking' as the lexicon lists.

In Psa 10:4 the plural noun 'devices, purposes' is what the wicked holds with the pride of his face: all his purposes are that there is no God; the lexicon lists 'purpose, device', and the verse gives the content as a denial of God.

In Gen 6:5, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7 (two occurrences) and Jer 4:14 the plural noun 'thoughts, devices' is what the wicked hold and plan: evil continually, schemes to wrong, thoughts against the speaker, an abomination to the Lord, to be forsaken, thoughts of iniquity, wicked thoughts that lodge; the sense is the planned or entertained thoughts of persons, evil in each.

In 1Ch 29:18, Psa 94:11, Pro 12:5 and Isa 66:18 the plural noun 'thoughts' is the thinking of persons as open to God and having a moral quality: kept toward the Lord, known as a breath, just in the righteous, known with their works; the sense is thoughts as the content of the mind that God knows.

In Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5, Mic 4:12 and Isa 55:8-9 the plural noun 'thoughts' is the Lord's own thinking: his thoughts toward us, very deep, not known by the nations, and in Isa 55:8-9 set against the thoughts of those addressed as higher; the sense is God's purposes and thinking.

In Job 20:2 the plural noun 'disquietings' with the possessive is the subject: his thoughts answer him because of his haste; it is a troubled, restless reflection, a word that the lexicon gives only as disquietings.

lexicon.lsj:
ὁ,
ἡ, τό, is, when thus written,
__A demonstrative Pronoun.
__B in Attic dialect, definite or prepositive Article.
__C in Epic dialect, the so-called postpositive Article, = relative Pronoun, ὅς, ἥ, ὅ.—The nominative masculine and feminine singular and plural, ὁ, ἡ, οἱ, αἱ, have no accent in codices and most printed books, except when used as the relative; but ὁ, ἡ, οἱ, αἱ differ only in writing from ὃ, ἣ, οἳ, α; the nominative forms of the article are said by Hdn.Gr.1.474 to be oxytone, and by [Refs 2nd c.AD+] in Aeolic dialect accusative to [Refs 8th c.BC+] genitive and dative dual τοῖιν [Refs 8th c.BC+]— In Doric dialect and all other dialects except Attic dialect and Ionic dialect the feminine forms preserve the old ᾱ instead of changing it to η, hence Doric dialect etc. ἁ, τάν, τᾶ; the genitive plural τάων contracts in many dialects to τᾶ; the genitive singular is in many places τῶ, accusative plural τώς, but Cretan dialect, etc., τόνς [Refs]; in Lesbian Aeolic dialect the accusative plural forms are τοὶς, ταὶς, [Refs]; dative plural τοῖς, ταῖς (or τοὶς, ταὶς, see above), [Refs]; ταῖσι as demonstrative, [Refs 7th c.BC+] Poets also used the Ionic dialect and _Epic dialect_ forms τοῖσι, ταῖσ; and in Trag. we find τοὶ μέν.., τοὶ δέ.., for οἱ μέν.., οἱ δέ.., not only in Lyric poetry, as [Refs 5th c.BC+]; but even in a trimeter, [Refs 5th c.BC+] {ὅ}; τὼ πόλεε Foed. cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+]; in [Refs 4th c.AD+] functions as genitive dual feminine, μεσακόθεν τοῖς κράναιυν [Refs 4th c.BC+] —in Elean and _Boeotian dialect_ ὁ, ἡ (ἁ), τό, with the addition of -ί, ={ὅδε}, ἥδε, τόδε, _nominative_ _plural_ _masculine_ τυΐ the following men, [Refs 3rd c.BC+] cf. Sanskrit demonstrative pronoun sa, sā, Gothic sa, sō, ONorse sá, sú, Old Latin accusative sum, sam (Enn.): —with τό [from *τόδ] cf. Sanskrit tat (tad), Latin is-tud, Gothic pata: —with τοί cf. Sanskrit te, Lithuanian tĩe, O[Refs 5th c.BC+] pá, etc.:—with τάων cf. Sanskrit tāsām, Latin is-tarum:— the origin of the relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (which see) is different.)
__A ὁ, ἡ, τό, DEMONSTR. PRONOUN, that, the oldest and in [Refs 8th c.BC+] the commonest sense: frequently also in [Refs 5th c.BC+], and sometimes in Trag. (mostly in Lyric poetry, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; τῶν γάρ.., τῆς γάρ.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; seldom in Attic dialect Prose, except in special phrases, see infr. VI, VII):
__A.I joined with a substantive, to call attention to it, ὁ Τυδεΐδης he—Tydeus' famous son, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; τὸν Χρύσην that venerable man Chryses, I.II: and so with appellative, Νέστωρ ὁ γέρων N.—thataged man, [Refs]; αἰετοῦ.. τοῦ θηρητῆρος the eagle, that which is called hunter, [Refs]; also to define and give emphasis, τιμῆς τῆς Πριάμου for honour, namely that of Priam, [Refs]; οἴχετ᾽ ἀνὴρ ὤριστος a man is gone, and he the best, [Refs]:—different from this are cases [Refs 8th c.BC+] if he would help the Trojans, but drive those back to the ships—I mean the Achaeans, where Ἀχ. is only added to explain τούς, compare [Refs]
__A.II frequently without a substantive, he, she, it, ὁ γὰρ ἦλθε [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.III placed after its Noun, before the Relat. Prons., ἐφάμην σὲ περὶ φρένας ἔμμεναι ἄλλων, τῶν ὅσσοι Λυκίην ναιετάουσι far above the rest, above those to wit who, etc., [Refs 8th c.BC+]; οἷ᾽ οὔ πώ τιν᾽ ἀκούομεν οὐδὲ παλαιῶν, τάων αἳ πάρος ἦσαν.. Ἀχαιαί such as we have not heard tell of yet even among the women of old, those women to wit who.., [Refs 8th c.BC+] —for the _Attic dialect_ usage see below
__A.IV before a Possessive pronoun its demonstrative force is sometimes very manifest, φθίσει σε τὸ σὸν μένος that spirit of thine, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.V for cases in which the Homeric usage approaches most nearly to the Attic, see below [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.VI ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.. without a substantive, in all cases, genders, and numbers, [Refs 8th c.BC+] properly refers to the former, ὁ δέ to the latter; more rarely ὁ μέν the latter, ὁ δέ the former, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: sometimes in Partition, the one.., the other.., etc.—The Noun with it is regularly in genitive plural, being divided by the ὁ μέν.., ὁ δέ.., into parts, ἠΐθεοι καὶ παρθένοι.., τῶν δ᾽ αἱ μὲν λεπτὰς ὀθόνας ἔχον, οἱ δὲ χιτῶνας εἵατο [Refs 8th c.BC+]: but frequently the Noun is in the same case, by a kind of apposition, ἴδον υἷε Δάρητος, τὸν μὲν ἀλευάμενον τὸν δὲ κτάμενον [Refs 8th c.BC+]: so in Trag. and Attic dialect, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; if the Noun be collective, it is in the genitive singular, ὁ μὲν πεπραμένος ἦν τοῦ σίτου, ὁ δὲ ἔνδον ἀποκείμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+]

__A.VI.3 ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δέ τις.. is used in Prose, when the Noun to which ὁ refers is left indefinite, ἔλεγον ὁ μέν τις τὴν σοφίαν, ὁ δὲ τὴν καρτερίαν.., ὁ δέ τις καὶ τὸ κάλλος [Refs 5th c.BC+]

__A.VII the following usages prevailed in Attic dialect Prose,
__A.VII.1 in dialogue, after καί, it was usual to say in nominative singular masculine καὶ ὅ; in the other cases the usual forms of the Article were used (see. ὅς [Refs 4th c.BC+] II.I and cf. Sanskrit sas, alternatative form of sa); so, in accusative, καὶ τὸν εἰπεῖν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.VII.2 ὁ καὶ ὁ such and such, τῇ καὶ τῇ ἀτιμίᾳ [Refs 5th c.BC+]: but mostly in accusative, καί μοι κάλει τὸν καὶ τόν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἀνάγκη ἄρα τὸ καὶ τό it must then be so and so, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; but τὰ καὶ τά now one thing, now another, of good and bad, τὸν δ᾽ ἀγαθὸν τολμᾶν χρὴ τά τε καὶ τὰ φέρειν [Refs 6th c.BC+]; so πάντα τοῦ μετρίου μεταβαλλόμενα ἐπὶ τὰ καὶ ἐπὶ τά, of excess and defect, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.VIII absolutely usages of single cases,
__A.VIII.1 feminine dative τῇ, of Place, there, on that spot, here, this way, that way, [Refs 8th c.BC+], etc.: also in Prose, τὸ μὲν τῇ, τὸ δὲ τῇ [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.1.b with a notion of motion towards, that way, in that direction, [Refs 8th c.BC+] —only poetry
__A.VIII.1.c of Manner, τῇ περ τελευτήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν in this way, thus, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.1.d repeated, τῇ μέν.., τῇ δέ.., in one way.., in another.., or partly.., partly.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.1.e relative, where, by which way, only Epic dialect, as [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.2 neuter dative τῷ, therefore, on this account, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.2.b thus, so, [Refs 8th c.BC+] precedes, be translated, then, if this be so, on this condition, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.VIII.3 neuter accusative τό, wherefore, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; also τὸ δέ absolutely, but the fact is.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; even when the τό refers to what precedes, the contrast may lie not in the thing referred to, but in another part of the sentence (compare above[Refs 5th c.BC+]; φασὶ δέ τινες αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ σοφῶν γεγονέναι· τὸ δὲ οὐκ ἦν but he was not, [Refs 1st c.BC+]

__A.VIII.6 ἐν τοῖς is frequently used in Prose with Superlatives, ἐν τοῖσι θειότατον a most marvellous thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι the very first, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν τοῖσι πρῶτος (πρώτοις codices) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; [Ζεὺς] Ἔρωτά τε καὶ Ἀνάγκην ἐν τοῖς πρῶτα ἐγέννησεν first of all, [Refs 2nd c.AD+] the greatest number of ships, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: also with adverbs, ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα [Refs 5th c.BC+]: in late Prose, also with Positives, ἐν τοῖς παράδοξον [Refs 1st c.BC+]
__B ὁ, ἡ, τό, THE DEFINITE ARTICLE, the, to specify individuals: rare in this signification in the earliest Gr., becoming commoner later. In [Refs 8th c.BC+] the demonstrative force can generally be traced, [Refs 4th c.BC+] I, but the definite Article must be recognized in places [Refs 8th c.BC+]: also when joined to an adjective to make it a substantive, αἰὲν ἀποκτείνων τὸν ὀπίστατον the hindmost man, [Refs 8th c.BC+].; also in τῶν ἄλλων [Refs]; also τὸ τρίτον[Refs]; τὸ μὲν ἄλλο for the rest,[Refs]—The true Article, however, is first fully established in 5th C Attic dialect, whilst the demonstrative usage disappears, except in a few cases, V. [Refs 4th c.BC+] —Chief usages, especially in _Attic dialect_
__B.I not only with common Appellats., adjectives, and Parts., to specify them as present to sense or mind, but also frequently where we use the Possessive pronoun, τὸ κέαρ ηὐφράνθην [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὴν κεφαλὴν κατεάγην my head was broken, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τοὺς φίλους ποιούμεθα we make our friends, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰς πόλεις ἔκτιζον they began founding their cities, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.b omitted with proper nounsand frequently with Appellats. which require no specification, as θεός, βασιλεύς, see at {θεός} [Refs] III; ἐμ πόλει in the Acropolis, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; compare Θράσυλος in [Refs]; or when the person spoken of is to be specially distinguished, Ζεύς, ὅστις ὁ Ζεύς whoever this Zeus is, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; and therefore properly omitted when a special designation follows, as Σωκράτης ὁ φιλόσοφος: seldom in Trag. with proper nouns, save to give peculiar emphasis, like Latin ille, ὁ Λάϊος, ὁ Φοῖβος, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.c Aristotle says Σωκράτης meaning the historical Socrates, as in [Refs] when he means the Platonic Socrates, as [Refs]
__B.I.d for Σαῦλος ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, etc., see at {καί} [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.2 in a generic sense, where the individual is treated as a type, οἷς ὁ γέρων μετέῃσιν.. λεύσσει [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__B.I.2.b frequently with abstract Nouns, ἥ τε ἐλπὶς καὶ ὁ ἔρως [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.3 of outstanding members of a class, ὁ γεωγράφος, ὁ κωμικός, ὁ ποιητής, ὁ τεχνικός, see at {γεωγράφος}, κωμικός, ποιητής, τεχνικός.
__B.I.4 with infinitives, which thereby become Substantives, τὸ εἴργειν prevention, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ φρονεῖν good sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+]infinitive, τὸ θεοὺς εἶναι the existence of gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ μηδένα εἶναι ὄλβιον the fact or statement that no one is happy, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.5 in neuter before any word or expression which itself is made the object of thought, τὸ ἄνθρωπος the word or notion man; τὸ λέγω the word λέγ; τὸ μηδὲν ἄγαν the sentiment 'ne quid nimis', [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ τῇ αὐτῇ the phrase τῇ αὐτῇ, [Refs 5th c.BC+] the opinion about the question 'who ought to rule', [Refs]; τὸ ἐὰν μένητε παρ᾽ ἐμοί, ἀποδώσω the phrase 'I will give back, if.. ', [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ ὀλίγοι the term few, [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__B.I.6 before relative clauses, when the Article serves to combine the whole relative clause into one notion, τῇ ᾗ φὴς σὺ σκληρότητι the harshness you speak of, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸν ἥμερον καρπόν.., καὶ τὸν ὅσος ξύλινος (i.e. καὶ τὸν καρπὸν ὅσος ἂν ᾖ ξύλινος) [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.I.7 before Prons.,
__B.I.7.a before the person Prons., giving them greater emphasis, but only in accusative, τὸν ἐμέ [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸν.. σὲ καὶ ἐμέ[Refs]
__B.I.7.b before the interrogative pronoun (both τίς and ποῖος), referring to something before, which needs to be more distinctly specified, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τῆς ποίας μερίδο; [Refs 4th c.BC+]; τοῖς ποίοις..; [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__B.I.7.c with τοιοῦτος, τοιόσδε, τηλικοῦτος, etc., the Article either makes the pronoun into a substantive, ὁ τοιοῦτος that sort of person, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; or subjoins it to a substantive which already has an Article, τὴν ἀπολογίαν τὴν τοιαύτην [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__B.I.8 before ἅπας, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also τὸν ἕνα, τὸν ἕνα τοῦτον, [Refs 4th c.BC+] see entry; and on οἱ ἄλλοι, οἱ πολλοί, etc., see at {ἄλλος} [Refs]
__B.I.9 the Article with the comparative is rare, if ἤ follows, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.II elliptic expressions:
__B.II.1 before the genitive of a proper name, to express descent, son or daughter, Θουκυδίδης ὁ Ὀλόρου (i.e. υἱός) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; Ἑλένη ἡ τοῦ Διός (i.e. θυγάτηρ) [Refs 5th c.BC+]: also to denote other relationships, e.g. brother, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἡ Σμικυθίωνος Μελιστίχη M.the wife of [Refs 5th c.BC+]; Κλέαρχος καὶ οἱ ἐκείνου Cl. and his men, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὁ τοῦ Ἀντιγένεος the slave of [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__B.II.2 generally, before a genitive it indicates a wider relation, as τὸ τῶν νεῶν, τὸ τῶν Ἑρμῶν, the matter of the ships, the affair of the Hermae, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ τοῦ Ἀρριβαίου πράσσειν to promote the interests of Arrhibaeus, [Refs]; τὸ τῆς τύχης,=ἡ τύχη, [Refs]; τὰ τῆς τύχης accidents, chance events, [Refs]; τὰ γὰρ φθιτῶν τοῖς ὁρῶσι κόσμος performance of the rites due to the dead befits the living, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ τῶν θεῶν that which is destined by the gods, [Refs 5th c.BC+] what regards me or thee, my or thy business or interests, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: and with genitive of [Refs 5th c.BC+] is frequently also, a man's word or saying, as τὸ τοῦ Σόλωνος [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὸ τοῦ Ὁμήρου as Homer says, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also τά τινος so-and-so's house, [NT+5th c.BC+]
__B.II.3 very frequently with cases governed by Preps.. αἱ ἐκ τῆς Ζακύνθου νῆες the ships from Zacynthus, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also τὰ ἐπὶ Θρᾴκης the Thrace-ward district, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ καταστρώματος matters on deck, [Refs]; τὰ ἀπ᾽ Ἀλκιβιάδου the proposals of Alcibiades, [Refs]; τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τύχης the incidents of fortune, [Refs]
__B.II.4 on μὰ τόν, μὰ τήν, etc., see at {μά} IV.
__B.II.5 in elliptical phrases, ἐπορευόμην τὴν ἔξω τείχους (i.e. ὁδόν) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἡ αὔριον (i.e. ἡμέρα), see at {αὔριον}; ἡ Λυδιστί (i.e. ἁρμονία) [Refs 4th c.BC+]; ὁ οἴκαδε πλοῦς [Refs 5th c.BC+], etc.; but τό stands absolutely with Advs. of time and place, when one cannot (as in the preceding instances) supply a substantive, as κἀκεῖσε καὶ τὸ δεῦρο [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὁ μὲν τὸ κεῖθεν, ὁ δὲ τὸ κεῖθεν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C as RELATIVE PRONOUN in many dialects; both in nominative singular masculine ὅ, as κλῦθί μοι, ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ὃ ἐξορύξη he who banishes him, [Refs]; and in the forms beginning with τ, especially in [Refs 8th c.BC+]: also in Ionic dialect Poets, ἐν τῷ κάθημαι [Refs 7th c.BC+]; τό [Refs]; τῶν[Refs]—Never in Comedy texts or Attic dialect Prose:—Epic dialect genitive singular τεῦ [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__D CRASIS OF ARTICLE:
__D.a Attic dialect ὁ, ἡ, τό, with ᾰ make ᾱ, as ἁνήρ, ἁλήθεια, τἀγαθόν, τᾄτιο; so οἱ, αἱ, τά, as ἅνδρες, τἀγαθ; also τοῦ, τῷ, as τἀγαθοῦ, τἀγαθῷ: ὁ, τό, οἱ, before e gives ου, οὑξ, οὑπί, οὑμός, τοὔργον, οὑπιχώριοι, etc.; also τοῦ, as τοὐμοῦ, τοὐπιόντο; but ἅτερος, θάτερον ([musical notation]), Ionic dialect οὕτερος, τοὔτερον (see. ἕτερος), Attic dialect feminine ἡτέρα, dative θητέρᾳ (see. ἕτερος); τῷ loses the iota, τὠμῷ, τὠπιόντι: ὁ, τό, before ο gives ου, as Οὁδυσσεύς, Οὑλύμπιος, τοὔνομα: ὁ, τό, etc., before αυ gives ᾱυ, αὑτός, ταὐτό, ταὐτῷ (frequently written ἁτός, etc. in Inscrr. and Papyrus); so τὰ αὐτά=ταὐτά, αἱ αὐταί=αὑταί: ἡ before εὐ gives ηὑ, as ηὑλάβεια: τῇ before ἡ gives θη, as θἠμέρᾳ: τὸ before ὑ gives θου, as θοὔδωρ for τὸ ὕδωρ.
__D.b other dialects: in their treatment of crasis these follow the local laws of contraction, hence, e.g., Doric dialect ὡξ from ὁ ἐξ [Refs 3rd c.BC+]; Ionic dialect ᾡσυμνήτης from ὁ αἰς-[Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὡυτή from ἡ αὐτή [Refs 1st c.AD+]

to_take_up.text: The surfaces of this group share one kind of meaning: forming or bringing forth within. The codes carry it as conceiving (H2029, whose Poel sense is 'to conceive, contrive, devise'; H3179; G4815), as being with child (H2030A) and as planning and devising (H2803I); the verses give both a child conceived (Jdg 13:7, Mat 1:23, Psa 51:5) and trouble or harm conceived or devised (Job 15:35, Psa 41:7).

The lexicon entries bear the grouping out only for part of the group: the codes of conceiving and being with child are H2029 (to conceive; the Poel sense is to contrive, devise; 5 occurrences), H3179 (to conceive), H2030A (pregnant), G4815 (to seize, conceive, help) and H2232 (to sow, the Niphal to be made pregnant), and the code of planning is H2803I (to plan, devise). G2192 (to have), G2602 (beg
Calling stands with the group in Isa 7:14 (call, 3 after), Mat 1:23 (5 after) and Luk 1:31 (7 after). In all three the calling of the child's name follows the conceiving and the bearing of a son.

Bearing stands with the group in six verses, 1 word after the member in Jdg 13:3, 13:5, 13:7 and Isa 7:14, 2 after in Mat 1:23 and 4 after in Luk 1:31. In every verse the bearing of a child is the second act of the pair, conceive and bear.

The surface 'conceive' carries nine codes in two senses, with one rhetorical use between them. The bodily conceiving of a child: H2232 (Num 5:28), H2029 (Jdg 13:3), H2030A (Jdg 13:5, 13:7, Isa 7:14), H3179 (Psa 51:5), and the Greek G4815 (Luk 1:31), G2192 with G1722 (Mat 1:23) and G2602 with G4690G (Heb 11:11). The figurative conceiving of trouble, chaff and mischief: H2029 in Job 15:35, Isa 33:11

The surface 'imagine' carries two codes: H2803I in Psa 41:7, which gives the sense (to devise the worst against the speaker), and H5921A, the preposition 'upon', which the unit aligns into the same word without carrying a sense.

Qualifiers stand with the devising group in four verses with negators (5 stored pairs). They reach words other than the member: 'defiled' in Num 5:28 (a woman not defiled shall conceive), 'borne' in Jdg 13:3 (barren, has not borne), and in Jdg 13:5 and 13:7 the things the woman must not do (a razor, wine, strong drink, unclean food). Entities are named in 8 of the 13 verses of the devising group, 7 different ones in 15 stored pairs (9 human, 6 divine). The divine are God (4), the Lord and Jesus; the human are Immanuel (3), Sarah (2), the woman and the child. The persons are those conceiving or conceived (Sarah, the woman, Immanuel), and the divine appear as the one who sends the angel or whose name 'God with us' the child bear

The direction does not change across the verses of the devising group. In Jdg 13:3, 13:5, 13:7, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 a messenger or the Lord announces to a woman that she will conceive and bear a son, and in Heb 11:11 Sarah received power to conceive; the conceiving runs from the woman to the child, and the divine entity is the source of the announcement.

may_rest_on_besides.text: In Num 11:12 and Judg 13:3 harah ('to conceive') is said of a woman's bearing of a child: Moses asks whether he conceived the people and gave them birth, a mother's acts set beside nursing, and the angel tells the barren woman, who has not borne children, that she will conceive and bear a son; conceiving is the beginning of the child.

In Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 harah ('to conceive') is not said of a child: what is conceived is trouble, chaff and mischief, and what is born of it is evil, stubble and iniquity; the verbs of pregnancy and birth are carried over to the devising of harm, the birth being the deed that follows the plan.

In Mat 1:23 the verb whose usual sense is 'to have, hold' stands in the future active, third singular, and carries 'become pregnant' only through the clause it stands in (the virgin, the bearing of a son that follows); the dictionary sense of the code is possession, not conception.

In Heb 11:11 the noun whose dictionary senses are 'foundation, a casting down' is the first member of a two-noun phrase that the verse gives as conceiving; it names the laying down of seed, and the lexicon itself lists 'conception in the womb' for this verse.

In Heb 11:11 the noun 'seed' stands in the genitive, the second member of the phrase that is rendered to conceive (with the casting down, G2602, in the same unit); here it is the male seed, which the lexicon lists for this verse as semen virile.

In Luk 1:31 the verb is in the future indicative, second person, with 'in your womb' and the bearing of a son after it; its sense here is 'become pregnant', one of the senses the lexicon lists for the code (Lk 1:24, 31, 36; 2:21).

In Jdg 13:5, Jdg 13:7 and Isa 7:14 the feminine adjective 'pregnant' is predicated of a woman and followed by the bearing of a son; the word names the state of being with child, and the ESV renders the announcement with the verb conceive.

In Num 5:28 the Niphal (the passive stem, as the morph HVNq3fs shows) of the verb 'to sow' means to be made pregnant, the sense the lexicon lists for the Niphal; the verse sets it as the result for a woman found clean.

In Psa 51:5 the Piel perfect, third feminine singular, of the verb 'to be hot' means to conceive in the sexual sense (the Piel sense the lexicon lists); its subject is the speaker's mother and its object the speaker, so it names the origin of his life.

In Psa 41:7 the Qal imperfect, third masculine plural, of the verb 'to think, plan' has the worst for the speaker as its object: the sense is 'to devise', the planning of harm by those who whisper together against him, the lexicon's 'to plan, devise'.

lexicon.lsj:
ἐν,
poetry ἐνί, εἰν, εἰνί [Refs 8th c.BC+], forms used by Epic dialect and Lyric Poets as the metre requires, but only as false reading in Trag., εἰν [Refs 5th c.BC+] ἰν [Refs]
__PREP. WITH DAT. AND ACC. Radical sense, in, into.
__A WITH DAT.
__A.I OF PLACE,
__A.I.1 in, νήσῳ ἐν ἀμφιρύτῃ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; with names of cities or islands, as ἐν Ἀθήνῃς, ἐν Τροίῃ, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; where ἐν is used, it = in the district of.., ὲν Ἐλευσῖνι [Refs] in my arms, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν αὑτῷ εἶναι to be in one's senses, be oneself, ἔτ᾽ ἐν σαυτῷ (variant -τοῦ) γενοῦ [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.1.b ἐν τοῖς ἰχθύσιν in the fish-market, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; so ἐν τοῖν δυοῖν ὀβολοῖν ἐθεώρουν ἄν in the two-obol seats, [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__A.I.2 elliptic, in such phrases as ἐν Ἀλκινόοιο [NT+8th c.BC+]; ἐν παιδοτρίβου, ἐν κιθαριστοῦ, at the school of.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν γειτόνων (see. γείτων) ἐν αὑτοῦ (αὑτῷ codex Rav.) [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.3 in, within, surrounded by, οὐρανὸς ἐν αἰθέρι καὶ νεφέλῃσι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν ὅπλοισι in or under arms, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also of particular kinds of arms, ἐν τόξοις, ἀκοντίοις, etc., equipped with them, uncertain in [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν μεγάλοις φορτίοις βαδίζειν καὶ τρέχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.4 on, at or by, ἐν ποταμῷ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; νευρὴ ἐν τόξῳ the string on the bow, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; κατεκλάσθη ἐνὶ καυλῷ ἔγχος was broken off at or by the shaft,[Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν οἴνῳ at wine, probably in [Refs 3rd c.BC+]
__A.I.5 in the number of, amongst, frequently in [Refs 8th c.BC+]; and with Verbs of ruling, ἐν δ᾽ ἄρα τοῖσιν ἦρχ᾽ [Refs 8th c.BC+] —for ἐν τοῖς with _superlative_, V. ὁ.
__A.I.5.b in the presence of, ἐν πᾶσι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; λέγειν ἐν ἀνδράσιν (of a woman) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; of a trial, διαγωνίζεσθαι, διαδικάζεσθαι ἔν τισι, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.6 in one's hands, within one's reach or power, νίκης πείρατ᾽ ἔχονται ἐν ἀθανάτοισι θεοῖσι [Refs 8th c.BC+], with infinitive, it depends on him to.., rests with him to.., ἔστιν ἐν σοὶ ἢ.. ἤ.. [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also ἐν τούτῳ εἰσὶν πᾶσαι αἱ ἀποδείξεις depend on this, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔν γ᾽ ἐμοί so far as rests with me, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also ἐν ἐμοί in my judgement, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν θεοῖς καλά in the eyes of the gods, [Refs]
__A.I.7 in respect of, ἐν πάντεσσ᾽ ἔργοισι δαήμονα φῶτα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν γήρᾳ σύμμετρός τινι in point of age.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν ἐμοὶ θρασύς in my case, towards me, [Refs]; ἡ ἐν τοῖς ὅπλοις μάθησις [Refs 5th c.BC+]; also οὐδὲν δεινὸν μὴ ἐν ἐμοὶ στῇ stop with me, [Refs]
__A.I.8 in a pregnant construction with Verbs of motion, into; implying both motion to and subsequent position in a place, ἐν κονίῃσι χαμαὶ πέσεν fell [to the dust and lay] in it, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν στήθεσσι μένος βαλεῖν[Refs 8th c.BC+]: in Trag. and Attic dialect, ἐν ποίμναις πίτνων [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν χωρίῳ ἐμπεπτωκώς [Refs 5th c.BC+]; later, with Verbs of coming and going, διαβάντες ἐν τῇ Σάμῳ [LXX+2nd c.AD+] is false reading in [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.9 πίνειν ἐν ποτηρίῳ to drink from a cup, [Refs 2nd c.AD+]
__A.I.10 ἄργυρος ἐν ἐκπώμασι silver in the form of plate, [Refs 1st c.AD+]; ἐμ φέρνῃ, ἐν θέματι, as a dowry, pledge, [Refs 1st c.BC+]
__A.I.11 in citations, ἐν τοῦ σκήπτρου τῇ παραδόσει in the passage of the [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.II OF STATE, CONDITION or POSITION:
__A.II.1 of outward circumstances, ἐν πολέμῳ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν γένει εἶναί τινι to be related to.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; of occupations, pursuits, ἐν φιλοσοφίᾳ εἶναι to be engaged in philosophy, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ ἐν ποιήσι γενόμενοι poets, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ ἐν τοῖς πράγμασι ministers of state, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ ἐν τέλει the magistrates, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὁ μάντις ἦν ἐν τῇ τέχνῃ in the practice of it, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.II.2 of inward states, of feeling, etc., ἐν φιλότητι, ἐν δοιῇ, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν ὀργῇ ἔχειν τινά to make him the object of one's anger, [Refs 5th c.BC+] to blame him, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν αἰτίᾳ εἶναι to have the blame, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.II.3 frequently with neuter adjective, ἐν βραχεῖ, ={βραχέως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν τάχει, ={ταχέως}, [Refs]; ἐν καλῷ ἐστί, ={καλῶς ἔχει}, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν ἀσφαλεῖ [ἐστί] [Refs]; ἐν εὐμαρεῖ [ἐστί] [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν ἴσῳ, ={ἴσως, ἐν ὁμοίῳ}, ={ὁμοίως}, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν κενοῖς, ={κενῶς}, [Refs] substantive, ἐν δίκᾳ, ={δικαίως}, opposed to παρὰ δίκαν[Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.III OF THE INSTRUMENT, MEANS or MANNER, ἐν πυρὶ πρήσαντες [Refs 8th c.BC+]; but in most cases the originally sense may be traced, to put in the fire and burn, infetters and bind, etc.; so ἐν πόνοις δαμέντα [Refs 4th c.BC+]; ἔζευξα πρῶτος ἐν ζυγοῖσι κνώδαλα[Refs]; also ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσιν or ἐν ὄμμασιν ὁρᾶσθαι, ἰδέσθαι, to see with or before one's eyes, i.e. have the object in one's eye, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; also ἐν λιταῖς by prayers, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν δόλῳ by deceit, [Refs]; ἐν λόγοις by words, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; especially with Verbs of showing, σημαίνειν ἐν ἱεροῖς καὶ οἰωνοῖς [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τὰ πραχθέντα.. ἐν.. ἐπιστολαῖς ἴστε ye know by letters, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.III.2 of a personal instrument, ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια [NT]
__A.IV OF TIME, ὥρῃ ἐν εἰαρινῇ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν τούτῳ (i.e. τῷ χρόνῶ) in this space of time, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν ᾧ (i.e. χρόνῳ) during the time that, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν ταῖς σπονδαῖς in the time of the truce, [Refs 5th c.BC+] in the course of the mysteries, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τραγῳδοῖς at the performance of.., [Refs 4th c.BC+]
__A.IV.b ἐν ἄρχοντι Μητροδώρῳ during the archonship of M., [Refs 2nd c.AD+]
__A.IV.2 in, within, ἐν ἡμέρῃ [Refs 5th c.BC+]; μυρίαις ἐν ἁμέραις in, i.e. after, countless days, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.V OF NUMBERS generally, ἐν δυσὶ σταδίοις within two stadia, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.V.2 with genitive of price, ἐν δύο ταλάντων [LXX]
__A.V.3 amounting to, προῖκα ἐν δραχμαῖς ἐννακοσίαις [Refs 2nd c.AD+]
__B WITH Acc., into, on, for, [Refs 4th c.AD+]; also poetry, ἐν πάντα νόμον [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__C WITHOUT CASE, AS adverb, in the phrase ἐν δέ..,
__C.1 and therein, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__C.2 and among them, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__C.3 and besides, moreover (not in Attic dialect Prose), [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__C.4 ἔνι, ={ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι}, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__D POSITION: ἐν frequently stands between its substantive and the adjective agreeing therewith, [Refs 8th c.BC+]: without an adjective, τῷ δ᾽ ἐν ἐρινεός ἐστι μέγας [Refs 8th c.BC+] between substantive and genitive, χόρτοις ἐν λέοντος [Refs]--One or more independent words sometimes come between the preposition and its dative, as in [Refs 8th c.BC+]; also in Prose, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__E IN COMPOSITION (joined with other words),
__E.I with Verbs, the preposition mostly retains its sense of being in or at a place, etc., with dative, or followed by εἰς.., or ἐν..: in such forms as ἐνορᾶν τινί τι, in translating, we resolve the compound, to remark a thing in one.
__E.I.b also, at a person, ἐγγελᾶν, ἐνυβρίζειν τινί.
__E.I.2 with adjectives, it expresses
__E.I.2.a a modified degree, as in ἔμπηλος, ἔμπικρος, ἔνσιμος, rather...
__E.I.2.b the possession of a quality, as in ἔναιμος with blood in it, ἐνάκανθος thorny: ἔμφωνος with a voice: ἔννομος in accordance with law, etc.
__E.II ἐν becomes ἐμ- before the labials β μ π φ ; ἐγ- before the gutturals γ κ ξ ; ἐλ- before ; ἐρ- before ; rarely ἐσ- before ; but Inscrr. and Papyri often preserve ἐν- in all these cases.

tree.text: (tr.) to have, hold, keep; (intr.) to be

pluperfect., ἐσχήκειν, to hold, Rev. 1:16; to seize, possess a person, Mk. 16:8; to have, possess, Mt. 7:29, and frequently ; to have, have ready, be furnished with, Mt. 5:23; Jn. 5:36; 6:68; to have as a matter of crimination, Mt. 5:23; Mk. 11:25; to have at command, Mt. 27:65; to have the power, be able, Mt. 18:25; Lk. 14:14; Acts 4:14; to have in marriage, Mt. 14:4; to have, be affected by, subjected to, Mt. 3:14; 12:10; Mk. 3:10; Jn. 12:48; 15:22, 24; 16:21, 22; Acts 23:29; 1Tim. 5:12; Heb. 7:28; 1Jn. 1:8; 4:18; χάραν ἔχειν, to feel gratitude, be thankful, 1Tim. 1:12; 2Tim. 1:3; Phlm. 7; to hold, esteem, regard, Mt. 14:5; Lk. 14:18, 19; to have or hold as an object of knowledge, faith, or practice, Jn. 5:38, 42; 14:21; 1Jn. 5:12; 2Jn. 9; to hold on in entire possession, to retain, Rom. 15:4; 2Tim. 1:13; Heb. 12:28; intransitive with adverbs or adverbial expression, to be, to fare, Mt. 9:12; Mk. 2:17; 5:23; Lk. 5:31; Jn. 4:52; Acts 7:1; 12:15; 15:36; 21:13; 2Cor. 10:6; 12:14; 1Tim. 5:25; 1Pet. 4:5; τὸ νῦν ἔχον, for the present; in NT ἔχειν ἐν γαστρι, to be pregnant, Mt. 1:18; as also ἔχειν κοιτην, Rom. 9:10; ἔχειν δαιμόνιον, to be possessed, Mt. 11:18; of time, to have continued, to have lived, Jn. 5:5, 6; 8:57; of space, to embrace, be distant, Acts 1:12; middle primarily to hold by, cling to; hence, to border upon, be next, Mk. 1:38; Lk. 13:33; Acts 20:15; 21:26; to tend immediately to, Heb. 6:9

lexicon.lsj:
ἔχω,

__A2nd pers. singular ἔχεισθα conjecture in [Refs 7th c.BC+]; 2nd pers. singular subjunctive ἔχῃσθα [Refs 8th c.BC+]imperfect εἶχον, Epic dialect ἔχον [Refs 8th c.BC+], Ionic dialect and poetry ἔχεσκον [Refs 8th c.BC+]future ἕξω, Epic dialect infinitive ἑξέμεναι [Refs 3rd c.BC+] (of momentary action, especially in sense check, see below [Refs 4th c.BC+], not found in Attic dialect Inscrr. or [Refs]; 2nd pers. singular σχήσησθα [Refs]aorist 1 ἔσχης α false reading in [Refs 3rd c.AD+]aorist 2 ἔσχον, imperative σχές [Refs 5th c.BC+] only in Oracle texts cited in [Refs 5th c.BC+]; subjunctive σχῶ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; 3rd.pers. plural σχοίησαν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; infinitive σχεῖν [Refs 8th c.BC+], Epic dialect σχέμεν [Refs] (in Alexandr. Gr. 3rd.pers. plural imperfect and aorist 2 εἴχοσαν [NT+3rd c.BC+], see at {Σχέθω}: perfect ἔσχηκα [Refs 5th c.BC+]; Epic dialect ὄχωκα is uncertain, see at {συνόχωκα}:—middle, imperfect εἰχόμην [Refs 5th c.BC+]: future ἕξομαι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; σχήσομαι[Refs 5th c.BC+]perfect passive παρ-έσχημαι in middle sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+]: aorist 2 ἐσχόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+], rare in Attic dialect except in compounds; imperative σχέο [Refs 8th c.BC+]lon947, etc.; infinitive σχέσθαι [Refs 8th c.BC+] —passive, future middle ἐν-έξομαι in passive sense, [Refs 5th c.BC+], frequently in compounds (συ-) [Refs 1st c.BC+]: aorist 1 ἐσχέθην [Refs 5th c.BC+]future middle σχήσομαι in passive sense, [Refs 8th c.BC+]: aorist 2 middle in passive sense, ἐσχόμην [Refs 8th c.BC+], participle σχόμενος [Refs 8th c.BC+]: perfect ἔσχημαι [Refs 2nd c.AD+]; also in compounds, frequently written -ίσχημαι, -ήσχημαι in codices of late authors. (I.-[Refs 5th c.BC+] seĝh- (cf. Sanskrit sáhate 'overpower', Gothic sigis 'victory', Gr. ἔχ- dissimilated from ἔχ-), reduced form sĝh-(σχ-), whence reduplicate ἴσχω (= si-sĝh-o) (which see): compare ἕκ-τωρ, ἕξω, ἕξι; but hέχ- [Refs]
__A Trans., have, hold:
__A.I possess, of property, the most common usage, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; οἵ τι ἔχοντες the propertied class, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὁ ἔχων a wealthy man, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; οἱ οὐκ ἔχοντες the poor, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔχειν χρέα to have debts due to one, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; to have received, θεῶν ἄπο κάλλος ἐ. [Refs 5th c.BC+]; πλέον, ἔλασσον ἔ.. (see. Hymns of vv.): in aorist, acquire, get, ὄνομα [Refs 5th c.BC+]: also future σχήσω, δύναμιν [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—passive, to be possessed, ἔντεα.. μετὰ Τρώεσσιν ἔχονται [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.I.2 keep, have charge of, ἔχον πατρώϊα ἔργα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; διαιτητῶν ἐχόντων τὰς δίκας having control of, [Refs 4th c.BC+]; to be engaged in, φυλακὰς ἔχον kept watch, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; σκοπιὴν ἔ. τινός for a thing, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἐν χερσὶν ἔ. τι (see. χείρ).
__A.I.2.b metaphorically, of a patient, οὐκ ἔχει ἑωυτόν is not himself, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.3 with accusative loci, inhabit, οὐρανόν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; haunt, [Νύμφαι] ἔχουσ᾽ ὀρέων αἰπεινὰ κάρηνα [Refs 8th c.BC+]; especially of tutelary gods and heroes, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; of men, πόλιν καὶ γαῖαν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; Θήβας ἔσχον (ἔσχεν codices) ruled it, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔχεις γὰρ χῶρον occupiest it, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; in military sense, ἔ. τὸ δεξιόν (with or without κέρας) [Refs 5th c.BC+]; of beasts, τὰ ὄρη ἔ. [Refs]
__A.I.4 have to wife or as husband (usually without γυναῖκα, ἄνδρα), οὕνεκ᾽ ἔχεις Ἑλένην καί σφιν γαμβρὸς Διός ἐσσι [Refs 8th c.BC+]; also of a lover, [Refs 5th c.BC+]:—in passive, τοῦ περ θυγάτηρ ἔχεθ᾽ Ἕκτορι [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.I.5 have in one's house, entertain, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.I.6 present participle with Verbs, almost, = with, ἤϊε ἔχων ταῦτα [Refs 5th c.BC+] —Prose use.
__A.I.7 of Place, ἐπ᾽ ἀριστερὰ ἔ. τι keep it on one's left, i.e. to keep to the right of it, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἐν δεξιᾷ, ἐν ἀριστερᾷ ἔ., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τοὺς οἰκέτας ὑστάτους ἔ. [Refs 5th c.BC+]: but in aorist, get, περιπλώοντες τὴν Λιβύην τὸν ἥλιον ἔσχον ἐς τὰ δεξιά [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.8 of Habits, States, or Conditions, bodily or mental, γῆρας λυγρὸν ἔ [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ὕβριν ἔ. indulge in.., [Refs], etc.; [Ἀφροδίτην[Refs 8th c.BC+]; κότον ἔ. τινί, ={κοτεῖσθαι},[Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἡσυχίην ἔ. keep quiet, [Refs 5th c.BC+] (future ἡσυχίαν ἕξειν [Refs 4th c.BC+] will not keep still for a moment, [Refs]; αἰτίαν ἔ. to be accused, [Refs 5th c.BC+]aorist, of entering upon a state, ἔσχεν χόλον conceived anger, [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔχειν τι κατά τινος have something against somebody, [NT]: —these phrases are frequently inverted, οὓς ἔχε γῆρας [Refs 8th c.BC+]; also of external objects, αἴθρη ἔχει κορυφήν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἔχῃ βέλος ὀξὺ γυναῖκα, of a woman in travail, [Refs 8th c.BC+]; λόγος ἔχει τινά with infinitive, the story goes, that.., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; and so in later Gr., [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ὡς ἂν λόγος ἔχῃ πρὸς ἀνθρώπους, ὅτι.. [Refs 1st c.AD+]:—passive, ἔχεσθαι κακότητι καὶ ἄλγεσι [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.I.9 possess mentally, understand, ἵππων δμῆσιν [Refs 8th c.BC+]; ἔχεις τ; do you understand? [Refs 5th c.BC+] attend! listen! [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔ. οὖν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἔχεις τοῦτο ἰσχυρῶ; [Refs 5th c.BC+]; know of a thing, μαντικῆς ὁδόν [Refs 5th c.BC+]; τινὰ σωτηρία; [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.10 keep up, maintain, καναχὴν ἔχε made a rattling noise, [Refs 8th c.BC+]
__A.I.11 involve, admit of, τά γ᾽ αἰσχρὰ κἀνθάδ᾽ αἰσχύνην ἔχει [Refs 5th c.BC+]; ἀγανάκτησιν, κατάμεμψιν, [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.I.12 of Measure or Value, τὸ Δαμαρέτειον.. εἶχε Ἀττικὰς δραχμὰς δέκα [Refs 2nd c.BC+]
__A.I.12.b Geometry texts, ἡ ἔχουσα τὰ κέντρα the (straight line) containing the centres, [Refs 3rd c.BC+]; ὁ κύκλος ἔχων τὸ πολύγωνον the circle containing (circumscribing) the polygon, [Refs]
__A.I.13 with doubleaccusative, Ὀρφέα ἄνακτ᾽ ἔχειν [Refs 5th c.BC+]
__A.II hold:
__A.II.1 hold, ἔ. χερσίν, ἐν χερσίν, μετὰ χερσίν, etc., see at {χεί; μετὰ γαμφηλῇσιν ἔ}.
